clue.text: Know-all going round bar is key detective

annotationWithheld.why: Know-all going round bar is key detective (6,4): C + LEVER (bar) + DICK (detective) gives the letters, but 'going round' and 'key' cannot both supply the C; one of them has no job, and no source gives the setter's parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Know-all going round bar is key detective

clue.text: Confronted with this, puny Sassenachs couldn't give a toss!

definitions.text: Confronted with this, puny Sassenachs couldn't give a toss!

parts.words: Confronted with this, puny Sassenachs couldn't give a toss!
parts.note: a weak Englishman could not throw the heavy pole tossed at Highland games; 'couldn't give a toss' is literal as well as slang for not caring

explanation.surface: Feeble English visitors do not care about something Scottish.
explanation.walkthrough: Sassenachs are the English, in Scots usage; Highland games include tossing a tree-trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heavy pole tossed end over end as a test of strength in Scottish games.

clue.text: Cosmetic I reportedly put on dog

indicators.note: put on means the first piece sits above the second in this down clue
reportedly means the pronoun I is used for how it sounds

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
to dog someone is to follow or shadow them

explanation.surface: Someone talks of putting on make-up before following a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is coloured make-up applied to the eyelids.

clue.text: Her first attempts to name her English teacher were initially deficient

definitions.text: Her first attempts to name her English teacher were initially deficient

parts.words: Her first attempts to name her English teacher were initially deficient
parts.note: the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion, taught English speech by Higgins; her early attempts did little at first, which echoes her surname

explanation.surface: A pupil's early efforts to address her language tutor fall short.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'name her' as 'name the woman whose English teacher was' Professor Higgins in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cockney heroine of Shaw's play, coached in speech by Henry Higgins.

clue.text: During last month his energy burst forth

indicators.note: During means the word his sits inside the month abbreviation

parts.note: DEC, December, is the last month of the year
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A man's vigour exploded late in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, to dehisce is for a seed pod to split open and release its contents.

clue.text: Bloomer put farm animals on edge

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits above the second in this down clue

parts.note: cows are farm animals
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: Livestock are made nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or a loaf, but here it is a flowering plant. 'put ... on edge' looks like an idiom for unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that blooms in spring with yellow flowers is a bloomer.

clue.text: No striker's backing direct method of payment

indicators.note: backing means the payment system's name is read from back to front

parts.note: BACS is the UK bank system for direct credits and debits

explanation.surface: A clue about how a non-striking worker is paid by direct transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns BACS round. BACS is the British interbank payment system, so 'direct method of payment' is a familiar phrase to UK readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike-breaker who keeps working during an industrial dispute is called a scab.

clue.text: Short pause required to identify butterfly

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark marking a brief break in a sentence
a species of British butterfly with ragged wings and a white mark under them

explanation.surface: A brief stop is needed to name an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark signals a brief pause; a British butterfly bears the same name.

clue.text: You might see Ben reload from this

definitions.text: You might see Ben reload from this

indicators.note: from this says the clue words are rebuilt from the letters of the answer, an anagram

explanation.surface: A soldier called Ben refilling his gun from a shoulder belt.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BEN RELOAD rearranged give the answer, and the whole clue describes it: a soldier reloads from his cartridge belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandoleer is a shoulder belt with loops for carrying cartridges.

clue.text: Self-righteous character ending research into our health upset

indicators.note: character ending picks out the last letter of research
upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A last research finding upsets a smug person's view of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character ending' gives H from research; 'upset' shuffles H with INTO OUR HEALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smugly convinced of their own moral superiority is sanctimonious.

clue.text: Flaw revealed by bishop replacing folio in European language

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter stands where another stood in the language name

parts.note: Flemish is the Dutch language spoken in Belgium
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman exposing a defect in a continental tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a mark or defect, a synonym for a flaw.

clue.text: Female holding party rejected this feller

indicators.note: holding means the female word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a woman is a female

indicators.note: rejected means the party word is turned back to front

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A woman refuses to have a man at her party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' is read as one who fells trees, not the slang for a man; 'this' points to the answer as the person meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester who cuts down trees is someone who fells them.

clue.text: Drop catches in authentic practice

annotationWithheld.why: Drop catches in authentic practice (9): HEARS (catches) inside REAL (authentic) gives the answer, but 'Drop' has no job in that parse and no source explains it

clue.text: Gilbertian princess with house in a state

parts.note: Princess Ida is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan heroine sets up home somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Extract from Pindar ode on riding display

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage from the Greek poet Pindar about horsemanship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of cowboy skills such as bronco riding.

clue.text: Preliminary part of course given to actors

indicators.note: given to joins the second piece on after the first

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside a golf fairway
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: An early bit of a training course is handed to performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preliminary part of course' reads as one phrase, but 'Preliminary' is the definition and the course is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, roughcast means roughly shaped, in an early unfinished form.

clue.text: Former priest converted with energy and skill

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: converted means the letters of priest are changed into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An ex-priest who changed faith brings energy and ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks religious beside 'priest' but rearranges PRIEST into PERTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is specialist skill or know-how.

clue.text: Popular sci-fi writer's second place in Scotland

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Jules Verne wrote early science fiction

explanation.surface: A famous science-fiction author's runner-up spot north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is a city in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Reportedly ailing church receives top award, causing displeasure

indicators.note: Reportedly says the word for ailing is used for its sound only

parts.note: ailing means unwell, sick

indicators.note: receives means the church abbreviation takes the award inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OM, the Order of Merit, is one of Britain's highest honours

explanation.surface: A sick churchman is given a top honour, though people are unhappy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' makes ailing count only for its sound, so a doubled letter can drop. The Order of Merit is a top British honour, in the monarch's personal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted, so it gives offence or displeasure.

clue.text: Scented leaves dramatic princess found in centre of pool

indicators.note: found in means the princess goes inside the central letters
centre of picks the middle letters of pool

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A stage princess discovered in the middle of a pond among fragrant foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dramatic' points to the stage: the princess is one of King Lear's daughters, and the pool supplies its two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb whose leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Outside northern city new pals embrace

indicators.note: Outside means the city letters go round the northern letter

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: new means the letters of pals are formed afresh

explanation.surface: Fresh friends hug outside a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London postal district; 'new' rearranges PALS into LASP.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclasp is to hold in one's arms, to hug.

clue.text: Hang about, remaining with husband

parts.note: over means left over, remaining

explanation.surface: Someone lingers, staying on with her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to linger or wait around near a place.

clue.text: Composer has change of heart, giving us a lift

indicators.note: change of heart says the middle letter of the composer's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: A composer has a change of mind and offers us a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of HOLST is its middle letter L; changing it to I gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a device for raising things, and as a noun it means a lift.

clue.text: Conclude a small number has escaped from raging fire

indicators.note: has escaped from means the number abbreviation leaves the blaze word

parts.note: an inferno is a raging fire
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Someone works out that a few people got out of a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small number' is the abbreviation NO, not a few people.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or reach a conclusion from evidence.

clue.text: Unconventional device for changing nature of motion

definitions.text: device for changing nature of motion
definitions.meaning: an engineering part, a disc mounted off-centre that turns rotary motion into back-and-forth motion

explanation.surface: An odd device altering how things move.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person is unconventional; in engineering an eccentric is an off-centre wheel converting rotation to reciprocation.

clue.text: Democrat upholding American's statement of belief

indicators.note: upholding means the second piece holds up the first from below in this down clue

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Democrat supporting an American's declaration of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' is a Native American people, not a US citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a formal set of religious beliefs.

clue.text: Cockney's quarter of a salad vegetable?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the aitch, so the H sounds go missing

parts.note: a quarter is half of a half

explanation.surface: A Londoner asks for a quarter of some green salad.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter of a thing is 'half half a', which a Cockney, dropping H, says 'alf 'alf a. Cockney is the working-class London dialect known for dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa, also called lucerne, gives sprouts eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: By hard work, gain acceptance, ultimately, in a plant

indicators.note: in means the final letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: chive is an onion-like herb plant

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of acceptance

explanation.surface: Through effort one wins acceptance at last in some industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E from acceptance; 'in' puts it inside A CHIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accomplish or attain something through effort is to reach it by your own labour.

clue.text: Spell Hilary, for example

definitions.meaning: a period of time, a stint
Hilary is the name of the spring session at Oxford University and of a law sitting

explanation.surface: Someone named Hilary spells something out.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person's name but is the Oxford spring academic session.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed period of time, such as an academic session.

clue.text: Dumbfounded son ends up ruined, without a pound

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the anagram goes round the pound sign
ruined says the letters of son ends up are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A son is ruined, left without even a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so the pound sign sits inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonplussed means utterly bewildered, so baffled that one cannot respond.
